answer: Neighborhood closure scoring: each agent's weight is capped by the density of distinct, mutually interacting peers within two hops, so isolated clusters never reach the influence zenith of well-connected regions. An attacker must grow and sustain a genuine interaction orchard around every fake node, paying ongoing bandwidth, latency, and coordination costs per identity rather than a one-time fee. Sybil clusters get filtered because their internal edges form a copper ring with no diverse external neighbors.
